abstract.t: A profile of RFC 4231 for nish/crypto/hmac (std/crypto/hmac.ts): HMAC () instantiated with SHA-256, SHA-384 and SHA-512. Every requirement quotes RFC 4231, the main source, and every RFC 4231 test vector for those three hash functions is held here.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.

nish/crypto/hmac exports one-shot HMAC-SHA-256, HMAC-SHA-384 and HMAC-SHA-512 over a key and a message, each as u8[], and a verify function for each that compares a tag with the one it computes. The construction is 's; the properties compare it with nish/crypto/sha256 and nish/crypto/sha512, the hash functions it is built on. RFC 4231 also defines HMAC-SHA-224, which nish/crypto/hmac does not export.

RFC 4231 has no binding sentence in the sense of BCP 14, so there is nothing to exclude. Two properties of the implementation lie outside what a functional test can observe and are held by nish's own tests instead. The verify functions compare through timingSafeEqual, whose loop tests/cases/ct_asm_k1_ct.ts holds to no branch on the data at 32 and 48 bytes after clang -O2 (docs/security/ct-verification.md, and docs/security/crypto-k1.md K1-8 for the verify functions themselves). The key blocks, hashed key, inner digest and hashers are wiped before return, held under -O2 by tests/wipes/crypto.js ("crypto_hmac crypto_hkdf: the wipes survive -O2"); the caller's own key array is recorded in docs/security/crypto-k1.md (K1-7) and docs/security/secret.md.

The module's other exports are out of scope here. hmacSha256Secret, hmacSha384Secret and hmacSha512Secret take the key as a Secret<u8[]>, which a property cannot construct; they compute the same function as the plain exports, and their wiping is held by nish's nish:secret tests. pbkdf2HmacSha256 is PBKDF2 (RFC 8018), which uses HMAC-SHA-256 as its PRF but is a different function, with its own vectors and none in RFC 4231. The classes HmacSha256, HmacSha384, HmacSha512, HmacSha256Scratch, HmacSha384Scratch and HmacKey are stateful, reusable forms of the same functions; a property here calls only functions, so they are left to nish's own tests.

section.name: Interface
section.sourcecode: // module: nish/crypto/hmac export const hmacSha256 = (key: u8[], data: u8[]): u8[] export const hmacSha384 = (key: u8[], data: u8[]): u8[] export const hmacSha512 = (key: u8[], data: u8[]): u8[] export const hmacSha256Verify = (key: u8[], data: u8[], tag: u8[]): boolean export const hmacSha384Verify = (key: u8[], data: u8[], tag: u8[]): boolean export const hmacSha512Verify = (key: u8[], data: u8[], tag: u8[]): boolean // module: nish/crypto/sha256 export const sha256 = (data: u8[]): u8[] // module: nish/crypto/sha512 export const sha384 = (data: u8[]): u8[] export const sha512 = (data: u8[]): u8[]

section.name: The Functions

blockquote.t: HMAC-SHA-256 is the realization of the HMAC message authentication code using the SHA-256 hash function

section.t: Note: the properties below hold hmacSha256 to the HMAC construction of over nish/crypto/sha256 (block length 64 bytes, ipad 0x36, opad 0x5c, a key longer than the block hashed first) and to a 32-byte tag, and hmacSha256Verify to accept that tag and refuse it with any one bit flipped.
section.sourcecode: // P-CONSTRUCTION-256 covers R-HMAC-SHA256 — HMAC-SHA-256 of a key of at most 64 bytes is the RFC 2104 construction over SHA-256 forall (key: u8[] /* 0..64 */, text: u8[] /* 0..200 */) => hmacSha256(key, text) === sha256(xor(key.concat(zeros(64 - key.length)), fill(92, 64)).concat(sha256(xor(key.concat(zeros(64 - key.length)), fill(54, 64)).concat(text))))

// P-LONG-KEY-256 covers R-HMAC-SHA256 — a key longer than 64 bytes gives the tag of its SHA-256 hash forall (key: u8[] /* 65..300 */, text: u8[] /* 0..100 */) => hmacSha256(key, text) === hmacSha256(sha256(key), text)

// P-VERIFY-ACCEPT-256 covers R-HMAC-SHA256 — hmacSha256Verify accepts the HMAC-SHA-256 tag forall (key: u8[] /* 0..200 */, text: u8[] /* 0..200 */) => hmacSha256Verify(key, text, hmacSha256(key, text))

// P-VERIFY-REJECT-256 covers R-HMAC-SHA256 — hmacSha256Verify refuses the HMAC-SHA-256 tag with any one bit flipped forall (key: u8[] /* 0..100 */, text: u8[] /* 0..100 */, bit: i32 /* 0..255 */) => !hmacSha256Verify(key, text, flipBit(hmacSha256(key, text), bit))

blockquote.t: HMAC-SHA-384 is the realization of the HMAC message authentication code using the SHA-384 hash function

section.t: Note: as for SHA-256, with SHA-384, a block length of 128 bytes and a 48-byte tag.
section.sourcecode: // P-CONSTRUCTION-384 covers R-HMAC-SHA384 — HMAC-SHA-384 of a key of at most 128 bytes is the RFC 2104 construction over SHA-384 forall (key: u8[] /* 0..128 */, text: u8[] /* 0..300 */) => hmacSha384(key, text) === sha384(xor(key.concat(zeros(128 - key.length)), fill(92, 128)).concat(sha384(xor(key.concat(zeros(128 - key.length)), fill(54, 128)).concat(text))))

// P-LONG-KEY-384 covers R-HMAC-SHA384 — a key longer than 128 bytes gives the tag of its SHA-384 hash forall (key: u8[] /* 129..400 */, text: u8[] /* 0..100 */) => hmacSha384(key, text) === hmacSha384(sha384(key), text)

// P-VERIFY-ACCEPT-384 covers R-HMAC-SHA384 — hmacSha384Verify accepts the HMAC-SHA-384 tag forall (key: u8[] /* 0..200 */, text: u8[] /* 0..200 */) => hmacSha384Verify(key, text, hmacSha384(key, text))

// P-VERIFY-REJECT-384 covers R-HMAC-SHA384 — hmacSha384Verify refuses the HMAC-SHA-384 tag with any one bit flipped forall (key: u8[] /* 0..150 */, text: u8[] /* 0..100 */, bit: i32 /* 0..383 */) => !hmacSha384Verify(key, text, flipBit(hmacSha384(key, text), bit))

blockquote.t: HMAC-SHA-512 is the realization of the HMAC message authentication code using the SHA-512 hash function

section.t: Note: as for SHA-256, with SHA-512, a block length of 128 bytes and a 64-byte tag.
section.sourcecode: // P-CONSTRUCTION-512 covers R-HMAC-SHA512 — HMAC-SHA-512 of a key of at most 128 bytes is the RFC 2104 construction over SHA-512 forall (key: u8[] /* 0..128 */, text: u8[] /* 0..300 */) => hmacSha512(key, text) === sha512(xor(key.concat(zeros(128 - key.length)), fill(92, 128)).concat(sha512(xor(key.concat(zeros(128 - key.length)), fill(54, 128)).concat(text))))

// P-LONG-KEY-512 covers R-HMAC-SHA512 — a key longer than 128 bytes gives the tag of its SHA-512 hash forall (key: u8[] /* 129..400 */, text: u8[] /* 0..100 */) => hmacSha512(key, text) === hmacSha512(sha512(key), text)

// P-VERIFY-ACCEPT-512 covers R-HMAC-SHA512 — hmacSha512Verify accepts the HMAC-SHA-512 tag forall (key: u8[] /* 0..200 */, text: u8[] /* 0..200 */) => hmacSha512Verify(key, text, hmacSha512(key, text))

// P-VERIFY-REJECT-512 covers R-HMAC-SHA512 — hmacSha512Verify refuses the HMAC-SHA-512 tag with any one bit flipped forall (key: u8[] /* 0..150 */, text: u8[] /* 0..100 */, bit: i32 /* 0..511 */) => !hmacSha512Verify(key, text, flipBit(hmacSha512(key, text), bit))

// P-TAG-LEN covers R-HMAC-SHA256, R-HMAC-SHA384, R-HMAC-SHA512 — the tags are 32, 48 and 64 bytes, the hash output, for any key and message forall (key: u8[] /* 0..200 */, text: u8[] /* 0..200 */) => hmacSha256(key, text).length === 32 && hmacSha384(key, text).length === 48 && hmacSha512(key, text).length === 64

section.name: The Test Cases

blockquote.t: Test with a key shorter than the length of the HMAC output.
Test with a combined length of key and data that is larger than 64 bytes (= block-size of SHA-224 and SHA-256).
Test with a truncation of output to 128 bits.

section.t: Note: the functions return the whole tag, so test case 5 (: a key of 20 bytes of 0x0c, the data "Test With Truncation") is written as a slice of it, its first 16 bytes.
section.sourcecode: // P-TRUNC-256 covers R-TRUNC, R-HMAC-SHA256 — RFC 4231 test case 5: the first 128 bits of HMAC-SHA-256 are a3b6167473100ee06e0c796c2955552b forall (n: i32 /* 16..16 */) => hmacSha256(fill(12, 20), utf8("Test With Truncation")).slice(0, n) === [a3 b6 16 74 73 10 0e e0 6e 0c 79 6c 29 55 55 2b]

// P-TRUNC-384 covers R-TRUNC, R-HMAC-SHA384 — RFC 4231 test case 5: the first 128 bits of HMAC-SHA-384 are 3abf34c3503b2a23a46efc619baef897 forall (n: i32 /* 16..16 */) => hmacSha384(fill(12, 20), utf8("Test With Truncation")).slice(0, n) === [3a bf 34 c3 50 3b 2a 23 a4 6e fc 61 9b ae f8 97]

// P-TRUNC-512 covers R-TRUNC, R-HMAC-SHA512 — RFC 4231 test case 5: the first 128 bits of HMAC-SHA-512 are 415fad6271580a531d4179bc891d87a6 forall (n: i32 /* 16..16 */) => hmacSha512(fill(12, 20), utf8("Test With Truncation")).slice(0, n) === [41 5f ad 62 71 58 0a 53 1d 41 79 bc 89 1d 87 a6]

blockquote.t: Test with a key larger than 128 bytes (= block-size of SHA-384 and SHA-512).
Test with a key and data that is larger than 128 bytes (= block-size of SHA-384 and SHA-512).

front.title: Identifiers and Test Vectors for HMAC-SHA-224, HMAC-SHA-256, HMAC-SHA-384, and HMAC-SHA-512

abstract.t: This document provides test vectors for the HMAC-SHA-224, HMAC-SHA-256, HMAC-SHA-384, and HMAC-SHA-512 message authentication schemes. It also provides ASN.1 object identifiers and Uniform Resource Identifiers (URIs) to identify use of these schemes in protocols. The test vectors provided in this document may be used for conformance testing. [STANDARDS-TRACK]

front.title: Key words for use in RFCs to Indicate Requirement Levels

abstract.t: In many standards track documents several words are used to signify the requirements in the specification. These words are often capitalized. This document defines these words as they should be interpreted in IETF documents. This document specifies an Internet Best Current Practices for the Internet Community, and requests discussion and suggestions for improvements.

front.title: Ambiguity of Uppercase vs Lowercase in RFC 2119 Key Words

abstract.t: RFC 2119 specifies common key words that may be used in protocol specifications. This document aims to reduce the ambiguity by clarifying that only UPPERCASE usage of the key words have the defined special meanings.
